Withdrawal: When you can't indulge in your maniacal behavior, you are overwhelmed by anxiety. You develop a lesser madness that can't be cured until you can return to your behavior or are cured from the addiction.

The fine arts for some are an interest, and even a passion. For you, they are an obsession. You must experience the highs crescendos and low dramatic tragedies. Experiencing great artistic endeavors inspires you and distills your focus for the coming day.

Relevant Skill: Perform or Artistry.

Indulge: You must experience a performance of some kind, be it an art display at a museum, an ally using their Perform skill or a concert or play. Roll a d20, with a result of 1-10 the performance was satisfactory but nothing special and you gain no bonus. With a result of 11-15 the performance was great and you gain a +2 morale bonus on Will saves for 24 hours. With a result of 16+ the bonus to will saves increases to +4. If an ally performs for you with the Perform skill, you gain a +1 bonus on this roll for every 5 of their check results. You may also increase the bonuses of this roll if no ally is involved by spending 5 gp per +1 bonus, the more expensive performances are more likely to inspire you. You may attempt to perform for yourself but you do not gain any bonuses from money or the check result as you gain more from hearing and learning other methods.

•

• Boon 1: You understand the bolstering power of music and can relate the salient details to an ally. Once per day, you may cast heroism as a spell-like ability.

• Boon 2: You can perform for your allies and bolster their morale. Three times per day, you can grant your allies a morale bonus to attack rolls, Will saves and skill checks equal to 1/4 your HD for 1 minute. Boon 3: Your ability to inspire your allies through your performances reaches immense heights. You may cast heroic invocation once per day as a spell-like ability.

Withdrawal: If you have not experienced a performance of some kind, you have difficulty focusing. To be able to cast spells or use point pools like inspiration or panache for any class ability you must make a Concentration check of 10 + the spell level or ½ their class level for pool point usage. If they fail, they cannot get the inspiration to perform the task, though they do not lose the point of Inspiration.

Be it to calm a constant anxiety, to fill an internal void, or to clear your mind, nothing gives you the same pleasure as engorging yourself with food and sweet drinks.

Relevant Skill: Craft (alchemy).

Indulge: Feast carelessly, alone or with your friends, until you are completely satiated. You have weight issues and are always encumbered. When a critical hit or sneak attack is scored on you, there is a 20% chance that the critical hit or sneak attack is negated and damage is instead rolled normally.

•

• Boon 1: There's nothing like food to make someone open their heart. You gain a morale bonus on all Bluff and Persuade checks equal to your character level.

• Boon 2: You gain DR 10 against slashing and piercing damage.

• Boon 3: You are immune to poisons. You also can always find poison in food or beverages as with detect poison.

Withdrawal: If you can't eat your fill, you feel weak, suffering a -2 penalty on all Strength- and Constitution?based die rolls.

Dice, cards, chess, whatever. You cannot stop. You cannot stand to lose. You could sell all your goods to stake them on the next game. But you swear you can tell who will be the winner next time…

Relevant Skill: Bluff.

Indulge: Play your favorite game with at least 1 other player. Roll 1d20. With a result of 1-10, you lose 1/10 of all your gold. With a result of 11-20, you win an equal amount. You also gain a +4 bonus on all Appraise checks for 24 hours.

•

• Boon 1: Winning is just a matter of calculating the odds. You may cast cleromancy once per day as a spell-like ability.

• Boon 2: Whoever makes the first move has an advantage. You gain Improved Initiative as a bonus feat. If you already have Improved Initiative, you instead add +10 ft. to your land speed.

• Boon 3: Knowing the rules allows you to find loopholes. You may cast time stop once per day as a spell-like ability.

Withdrawal: If you can't play, you can't sleep or rest properly. You are fatigued and require double the usual time to regain your spells.

You are dependent on alcoholic drinks or other drugs. These blur your judgment but can give you surprising insights and resistance to external control.

Relevant Skill: Heal.

Indulge: Consume a massive dose of your chosen beverage or drug. You gain all the bonuses and damages listed for that substance. You also gain a +4 bonus against mind-affecting and language-dependent effects for 24 hours.

•

• Boon 1: Once per day, you can go on a rampage of intoxicated fury, functioning as the blood rage spell at a caster level equal to your character level.

• Boon 2: Your mind can work at an accelerated speed while you are under the effect of your chosen substance. Three times per day, you can roll twice any ability check or skill check involving a mental ability and take the better result.

• Boon 3: Your altered state of mind has opened the doors of perception for you, and leaves you in a psychedelic state that almost transcends space and time. You can cast foresight on yourself only as a spell-like ability once per day.

Withdrawal: You suffer the effects of a moderate addiction to your chosen substance. This addiction can't be cured by any amount of consecutive saves.
feat-battle-performance-combat:
You can play your instrument and use it as a weapon at the same time.

Prerequisites: Proficiency in a musical instrument weapon or Catch Off-Guard and Equipment Trick (instrument), bardic performance or raging song class feature, Perform 1 rank.

Benefit: Whenever you make a full attack with a musical instrument used as an improvised weapon or a normal weapon while you are maintaining a bardic performance, you can maintain the bardic performance for that round without expending one of your rounds of performance for the day. In addition, while you wield a musical instrument as a weapon, the time required to begin a bardic performance or switch from one bardic performance to another is reduced by one step (from a standard action to a move action, from a move action to a swift action, and from a swift action to an immediate action).
feat-forbidden-vigilante-knowledge:
You delve into powers beyond the capacity of other dilettantes and dabblers.

Prerequisite: Magical limit break vigilante talent, spellcasting class ability which removes access to spells.

Benefit(s): You are treated as though the 7th level spells of your spell list were on your spell list (a cabalist would gain access to 7th level witch spells).

Special: If you select the magical limit break vigilante talent a second time, you also treat 8th level spells of your spell list as though they were on your spell list.
feat-indefatigable-drummer:
A smile is not needed to keep the rhythm—stamina is.

Benefit: Add your Constitution modifier to Perform (percussion) skill checks instead of your Charisma modifier.
feat-musicians-grace-combat:
You can dance and flourish while smashing your enemies on the head with a lute or a flute.

Prerequisites: Proficiency in a musical instrument weapon or Catch Off-Guard and Equipment Trick (instrument), Weapon Finesse, bardic performance or raging song class feature, Perform 5 ranks.

Benefit: When using a musical instrument as an improvised weapon or a normal weapon, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier on melee attack and damage rolls. A light or one-handed instrument weapon is treated as a light or one-handed piercing weapon for all feats and class abilities that require such a weapon (such as a duelist's precise strike ability). The instrument must be fit for a creature of your size.
feat-shared-identity:
Share another's social talents.

Prerequisite(s): Dual identity class feature.

Benefit(s): You and another creature with this feat can choose to share each other's social and vigilante identities. This allows you to impersonate and use that creature's social and vigilante identities as if they were your own, as well as allowing them access to yours as if it were their own.
feat-shifting-weakness:
You can manipulate the biology of your symbiote to render it less vulnerable to harm.

Prerequisite: Symbiotic slayer 5th.

Benefit(s): Once per week, you can spend 8 hours to change your symbiote's vulnerability to another energy type.

Normal: You cannot change your symbiote's vulnerability.
feat-signature-talent-combat:
You really focus on some of your talents.

Prerequisite(s): Vigilante level 2nd.

Benefit(s): Select one vigilante talent, even if you don't currently possess it. You reduce any level requirement to select it and vigilante talents which require it as a prerequisite by 2. You can also select 1 of the following benefits:

• If the vigilante talent has a limited number of uses per day, you gain 1 additional use of it per day.

• If the vigilante talent allows a saving throw, increase the DC by +1.

• If the vigilante talent requires an attack roll or grants you a feat, you gain a +1 on attack rolls with that talent or when using that feat with an attack roll.

• If the vigilante talent would provide a benefit at a higher level, you treat your vigilante talent as 2 levels higher for the purposes of its effects.

Special: You can select this feat multiple times, either selecting a different vigilante talent or gaining two more benefits from this feat for a vigilante talent which you have already selected.
feat-sniper-bolts:
Your mystic bolts can strike at distant foes.

Prerequisite: Mystic bolts class feature.

Benefit(s): Increase the range of your mystic bolts by 15 feet. At 6th level and every 6 levels afterwards, the range of your mystic bolts increases by another 15 feet.
feat-splash-sniper-combat:
Even splash weapons can catch your foes off guard and vulnerable.

Prerequisite: Hidden strike +1d8 or sneak attack +1d6.

Benefit(s): You can deal hidden strike or sneak attack damage with a splash weapon, although the damage die of the hidden strike or sneak attack is reduced by 1 step. The attack must qualify for dealing hidden strike or sneak attack damage (such as against a flat-footed or unaware target) and be directed at a creature rather than a square. Also, when you throw a splash weapon, if only a single creature is providing soft cover to your target, your target does not receive the +4 bonus to AC.

Normal: You cannot deal hidden strike or sneak attack damage with a splash weapon.

Special: Hidden strike and sneak attack damage is unaffected by the Concentrated Splash feat.
feat-studious-dilettante:
Whether you are an Investigator or not, you are versed in one particular course of study.

Prerequisite(s): Int 13, Skill Focus with the focus skill of the course of study selected for this feat (see below), character level 3rd.

Benefit(s): Select one course of study listed for a legendary investigator. You must have Skill Focus in the focus skill related to the selected course of study (for example, Perform for the Arts course of study). This course of study cannot be one you already have. You gain one first-level ability granted by the selected course of study. For purposes of using that ability, treat your legendary investigator level as equal to your character level – 2, even if you have levels in legendary investigator. You do not gain any of the other abilities from the selected course of study.
feat-touch-of-death:
You can channel your ki to disrupt the flow of life force through a target's body.

Prerequisite(s): Ki class feature, Improved Unarmed Strike, base attack bonus +5, assassin level 1st.

Benefit(s): When using the death attack ability with an unarmed strike, you can expend ki to increase the DC. Every point of ki spent increases the DC by 1. You can spend a maximum number of points equal to half your assassin level.
feat-treacherous-gambit-combat:
You share your good fortune with allies.

Prerequisite(s): Bestow Luck.

Benefit(s): You gain an extra daily use of either your Defiant Luck or Inexplicable Luck feat, which you must share with an ally. In addition, you can grant additional uses of your Inexplicable Luck to allies by expending one use of mythic power each time you wish to use an immediate action to Bestow Luck.
feat-vigilante-casting-savant:
You gain a masked talent.

Prerequisite(s): Vigilante level 5th, must have an archetype with the alchemy or spellcasting class feature.

Benefit(s): You gain a vigilante talent.

Special: You cannot select this feat if you possess the Vigilante Savant feat.
feat-vigilante-savant:
You gain a masked talent.

Prerequisite(s): Vigilante level 7th.

Benefit(s): You gain a vigilante talent, treating your vigilante level as half when determining for which vigilante talents you can select with this feat.

Special: You cannot select this feat if you possess the Vigilante Casting Savant feat.
feat-violent-child:
You blend the magical with the martial.

Prerequisite: Magical child 1st.

Benefit(s): Add 1 spell per spell level from the magus spell list to the unchained summoner spell list with the magical child vigilante archetype.

Special: A magical child can choose to gain this feat in place of their 1st-level social talent. This feat can be selected multiple times, each time adding 1 new spell per level.
feat-viscous-poison:
You can make your sticky poison even stickier.

Prerequisite(s): Sticky poison alchemist discovery, assassin level 1st.

Benefit(s): You can use your poison expertise to increase the duration of sticky poison. When the viscous poison is applied to a weapon, the weapon remains poisoned for an additional number of rounds equal to half your assassin level (minimum 1).

Normal: The sticky poison alchemist discovery allows the weapon to remain poisoned for a number of rounds equal to your Intelligence modifier.
feat-wise-vigilante:
Your contemplative insight and indomitable will rule your talents.

Prerequisite: Vigilante 1st.

Benefit(s): You use your Wisdom instead of your Charisma for any vigilante ability you gain, such as the save DCs of your vigilante talents or other abilities gained from vigilante archetypes except for spellcasting or alchemy.

Special: This feat must be selected at 1st level, or before your first level of vigilante. A vigilante can choose to gain this feat in place of their 1st level social talent.

Special: You cannot select this feat if you possess the Genius Vigilante feat.
feat-able-sniper-combat:
You have trained at keeping hidden while sniping from afar.

Prerequisite(s): Dex 13, Stealth 3 ranks

Benefit(s): You gain a +2 bonus on ranged attack rolls against flat-footed creatures that are a minimum of 30 feet away. Additionally, you gain a +4 bonus to Stealth checks made to hide again after you have made an ranged attack roll while hiding.
feat-abnormal-interfacing-akashic:
Prerequisite(s): Ability to shape at least one 1 veil.

Benefit(s): Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. You may use the chosen ability score in place of one of the other ability scores for the purpose of veilweaving.

You gain 1 point of essence.

Special: You may select this feat multiple times. Each time beyond the first, select a class which grants the ability to shape one or more veils as a class feature. You may use the chosen ability score in place of one of the other ability scores for the purpose of any class features from the class. Each additional instance of this feat also grants 1 point of essence.
feat-acquired-immunity:
Benefit(s): Choose a number of poisons or diseases with unique names equal to your Constitution modifier. You become immune to those specific poisons or diseases. You may select magical diseases with this feat.

Special: This feat can be selected multiple times, each time selecting an additional number of poisons or diseases.
feat-adaptable-item-slot: Benefit(s): You may spend a move action to remove a non-cursed item from a magic item slot or cybertech slot and replace it with another item or cybernetic in your possession which can be put in the same slot and that has been in your possession for at least 24 hours.
feat-adaptable-transfer:
Prerequisite(s): Tinkern sphere ((computation) package).

Benefit(s): You may transfer routines you craft into gizmos created by others, constructs with the robot subtype, and any technological item which uses charges. If a robot has an AI routine installed in this way, it gains the aggregate template for as long as the AI remains installed. A robot must be willing or helpless for you to transfer an AI routine into it. A robot's effective gizmo level is equal to its CR, while a technological item's effective gizmo level is equal to the item's Craft DC -15.

Note: This feat may not be acceptable for all campaigns.

Consult with your GM before taking this feat.
feat-additional-invincibility:
Your armor sheds the mightiest blows.

Prerequisite(s): Armored invincibility class feature.

Benefit(s): You gain an additional use of your armored invincibility class feature.

Special: You can select this feat multiple times, each time gaining an additional use of your armored invincibility class feature.
feat-additional-shadow:
Your shadows flow from your inner power.

Prerequisites: Shadow copy class feature.

Benefit(s): Whenever you use your shadow copy class feature, you create an additional shadow copy.
feat-advanced-breath-weapon-breath:
Breath Feats: A new category of feats, these feats serve to alter a wyrmtouched's breath weapon. Some of these feats reduce the damage die of your breath weapon while being used, indicated on the following table: This reduction applies to all damage dice the breath weapon deals (a 5th level wyrmtouched with 14 Constitution who applied the Breath Weapon Artisan feat to their breath weapon would deal 2d4+2 damage rather than 2d6+2). These feats can be combined, but the reduction to the breath weapon's damage die is cumulative and a breath feat cannot be applied if it would reduce the damage of a breath weapon below 1d1. Breath feats are marked with the [Breath] tag. Dragons are treated as though they had the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purpose of qualifying for breath feats and treat their hit dice as their character level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.

Your breath weapon hinders foes in ways others cannot.

Prerequisite(s): Expanded Breath Weapon, character level 5th.

Benefit: If a creature fails its saving throw against your breath weapon, it also suffers the following effects for a number of rounds equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1):

• Acid: The foe is sickened

• Cold: The foe is fatigued

• Electric: The foe is dazzled

• Fire: The foe catches fire

• Bludgeoning: The foe takes a -2 penalty to all saving throws

• Piercing: The foe's base land and flight speed is reduced by half

• Slashing: The foe takes an amount of bleed damage equal to 1/2 your hit dice

• Negative Energy: The foe is shaken

• Sonic: The foe is deafened

Using this feat reduces the damage die of your breath weapon by 2 steps.
feat-aggravated-burns-combat: Benefit(s): Ongoing damage you deal from your attacks, spells, or other abilities ignores any energy resistance that targets possess.
feat-ai-summoner-champion:
Prerequisites(s): Conjuration sphere, Tinker UEn sphere ((computation) package).

Benefit(s): When you summon your companion, you may summon it as an AI rather than a manifested creature.

In order to summon an AI companion, you must have an eligible gizmo or other item (if you possess the Adaptable Transfer* feat) within range of the summon.

An AI version of a companion has the same skill ranks, mental ability scores, base saves, spheres, talents, and feats of the companion. An AI companion can take its normal suite of actions each round without needing you to spend additional actions commanding it regardless of its Intelligence score.

Special: If you possess the Call Planar Creature talent, you may transform a called creature into an AI once it agrees to your terms. An AI version of a called creature has the same skill ranks, mental ability scores, base saves, spheres, talents, spells, spell-like abilities, and feats of the creature. An AI companion can take its normal suite of actions each round without needing you to spend additional actions commanding it regardless of its Intelligence score. If you possess the Hostile Takeover* feat, you may attempt to summon an AI companion into an unwilling or attended object. The target or its owner is allowed a saving throw to resist the effect against your Conjuration sphere DC, and the AI companion is not summoned on a successful save.
feat-akashic-mechanisms-akashic-combat:
Prerequisite(s): Android or forgeborn.

Benefit(s): You may invest essence into your nanite surge racial trait to gain an additional use per day for each point invested or invest essence into your fearless, strange mind, natural armor, crystal skin, memory matrix, or constructed racial traits (individually) to increase any of their bonuses by 1 for each point invested.

You gain one point of essence.
feat-akashic-supply-akashic:
Benefit(s): You gain the ability to invest essence into a technological weapon you are carrying. For every point of essence invested, you may make one attack per round with that weapon which does not consume charges and which ammunition is magically generated for the attack. This ability does not enable you to make additional attacks per round with a weapon or make use of non-weapon items without consuming charges. You must load the generated ammunition normally, and the generated ammunition cannot be of any special materials or particularly sophisticated design (such as nanite canisters).

You gain one point of essence.
feat-aligned-focus:
Your connection to your magic manifests most strongly in spells that share your alignment.

Benefit: You increase the save DCs of spells you cast with an alignment descriptor that matches your alignment on at least one axis by 1.
feat-aligned-spell-metamagic:
Those whom your deity favors have nothing to fear from you.

Prerequisite(s): chaotic, evil, good, or lawful alignment; Spellcraft 10 ranks.

Benefit(s): This feat works as Selective Spell, except rather than choosing the targets that are excluded from the spell's effect, you select an alignment you have when casting an aligned spell. All targets who share this alignment with you are automatically excluded from the spell's effect, regardless of their number. You may decide whether to inflict no damage or half damage to creatures who are neutral with respect to the chosen alignment axis (if the aligned spell doesn't inflict damage, a neutral creature would get a +4 bonus on its saving throw instead of half damage). An aligned spell uses up a spell slot 2 levels higher than the spell's actual level.

An aligned spell must have a duration of instantaneous but has not to be a spell with an area of effect.
feat-always-a-threat-combat:
You can be ready for a fight in an instant.

Prerequisites: Quick Draw.

Benefit(s): When carrying a light or one-handed melee weapon, even if it is sheathed or stowed you threaten adjacent squares in melee. Additionally, whenever an opponent provokes an attack of opportunity from you, you may draw a light or one-handed melee weapon as part of that attack of opportunity. The target of this attack is considered flat-footed. You must have at least one hand free to benefit from this feat.

Normal: If you are unarmed and do not possess the Improved Unarmed Strike feat you are not considered to be threatening adjacent squares in melee.
feat-angels-darling:
Benefit(s): Whenever you consume the angel's whispers* stimulant, you gain a caster level equal to 1/2 your character level (if you do not already possess a higher caster level), an MSB equal to your character level, an MSD equal to 11 + your character level, and a pool of spell points equal to twice the number of talents gained from the stimulant.

You lose both of these benefits when the effects of angel's whispers wears off. If you do not have a casting tradition, you use Charisma as your casting ability modifier.
feat-arms-of-the-deep-mythic:
Your lashing strikes reach up from the water to strike from all directions.

Prerequisite(s): Large or larger size, two or more natural weapons, swim speed.

Benefit(s): While you are in the water, you gain the benefit of flanking whenever an ally threatens an enemy that is threatened by you. In addition, if you attack the same creature with two or more natural weapons, you provide the benefits of flanking to yourself against that target for each attack after the first.
feat-assassins-avatar:
You can share your killing expertise with your eidolon, allowing it to act as your proxy.

Prerequisite(s): Bond senses class feature, eidolon class feature, assassin level 3rd.

Benefit(s): You can increase your bond with your eidolon and not only share its senses but provide it with your deadly skills. While using the bond senses feature, your eidolon can use any of your assassin class features for a number of rounds equal to your assassin level. These rounds need not be consecutive. While using this feat, you must maintain concentration in order to share your abilities with your eidolon. Breaking concentration immediately ends the effects of this feat, but not those of the bond senses feature.
feat-assassins-draw:
You have practiced a deadly drawing strike for hidden weapons.

Prerequisite(s): Dex 17, Sleight of Hand 3 ranks, Quick Draw

Benefit(s): Once per round, if you draw a light weapon and attack in the same round, the target is considered flat-footed against the first attack made after drawing the weapon. Once a creature has been affected by this feat, they are immune to its effects for 1 minute.
feat-assassins-grace-combat:
You are very adept at dealing a finishing blow.

Prerequisite(s): sneak attack +5d6

Benefit(s): You may deliver a coup de grace against a target that is unaware of you, even if they are not helpless. You only add half the minimum damage that could be dealt by your sneak attack dice to the coup de grace DC when using this feat. The target must be completely unaware that you are a threat, abilities such as uncanny dodge can foil this feat, as can the target being aware of an invisible threat.
feat-astral-mechanics-psionic:
Prerequisites(s): Technologist*, ability to manifest astral construct.

Benefit(s): When you manifest astral construct, you may instead manifest an astral robot. Astral robots are identical to astral constructs, save that they have an intelligence score of 10, a number of skill points equal to twice their Hit Dice, and the robot subtype. The robot treats any skills you have ranks in as class skills. This does not grant the astral robot any robot upgrades or feats.
feat-astral-upload-psionic:
Prerequisites(s): Astral Mechanics*, Technologist*, ability to manifest astral construct.

Benefit(s): When you manifest astral construct and create an astral robot, you may augment the power as follows:

Augment By spending 4 additional power points, you may upload an AI from a storage bay or other receptacle in your possession into the astral robot. The astral robot gains the aggregate template alongside all of the benefits of the AI that was uploaded into it. You cannot use this ability to upload an AI whose CR exceeds your manifester level. If the astral robot is destroyed, the AI returns to your storage bay.
feat-attuned-arms-combat: Benefit(s): Select any number of combat feats that require you to choose a type of weapon (such as Weapon Focus and Weapon Specialization). You are treated as having the selected feats for all the weapons you have crafted that are legal choices for those feats. You are not considered to have those feats with these weapons for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.
feat-aura-study:
Despite your fixation on alternative tactics, you can still command the aura of a legend.

Prerequisite(s): Reduced commander's aura class feature.

Benefit(s): Select 1 aura you would normally gain from the commander's aura class feature except for destructive counsel, instantly gaining access to it.

Special: You can select this feat more than once, each time selecting a different aura.
feat-avid-spellbook-reader-mythic:
You can retain whole magical tomes in your memory.

Prerequisite: Avid Spellbook Reader.

Benefit: Your bonus on Spellcraft checks from Avid Spellbook Reader doubles, and you can forfeit the requisites for gaining the boons from your preparation rituals known. You can gain the boons for one more ritual at the same time by expending one use of mythic power.
feat-bait-and-switch-combat:
Your cunning bladework can turn the tables on your enemies.

Prerequisite(s): Swap Places, Switchblade, Weapon Finesse, positioning attack rogue talent.

Benefit(s): When you use the Switchblade feat and you hit our target, you can attempt a combat maneuver to reposition the target as a swift action. If the maneuver succeeds, you can force the target to move into your space while you take a 5-foot step to move into the space it has just left. The target's movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity unless you have the Greater Reposition feat. If your maneuver fails, you can still use your Switchblade feat to swap places with a willing adjacent ally.
feat-bane-spell-metamagic:
Your spells have greater power against creatures of a chosen type.

Prerequisite(s): Knowledge (see text) 3 ranks

Benefit(s): Choose one type of creature (and subtype, if a humanoid or outsider). Any spell you cast affects creatures of that type more strongly. Your caster level is increased by 1 for determining the spell's effects and duration against creatures of that type, though the spell's range, area, and number of targets are not affected. In addition, your save DCs are increased by 1 for creatures of that type and spells that deal hit point damage add +1 to each damage die against those creatures. A bane spell has its normal effects against creatures of other types (and subtypes). Against creatures other than the chosen type, the spells effects and duration are treated as if your caster level was 1 lower and the save DC and damage per die are likewise reduced by 1. A bane spell uses up a spell slot one level higher than the spell's normal level.

In order to select this feat, you must have at least 3 ranks in a Knowledge skill that is used to identify creatures of the chosen type and their abilities. Thereafter, you can prepare a bane spell that affects creatures of any type for which you have at least 3 ranks in the appropriate Knowledge skill. You need not take this feat more than once to affect creatures of different types, and you can prepare bane spells of more than one type simultaneously as long as you have at least 3 ranks in each appropriate Knowledge skill. You must specify a type (and subtype, if a humanoid or outsider) for each bane spell you prepare or spontaneously cast.
feat-battleborn:
The battlefield calms your mind and hones your spirit.

Prerequisite(s): Base Attack Bonus +3 or Wis 13+, Iron Will.

Benefit(s): When in combat you gain a +2 bonus on saves against all mind-affecting or emotion spells and effects, in addition the DC of any demoralize attempt made against you has its DC increased by 4.
feat-battledancing-combat-mythic:
Nothing can hinder your flowing movements in combat.

Prerequisite: Battledancing.

Benefits: You can use Battledancing when wearing any type of armor. If you are wearing armor that's made mostly of cloth, the total bonus from Battledancing increases to +4 and you can divide it as you like among 2, 3, or 4 opponents.
feat-battledancing-combat:
You use graceful movements and flowing garments to hinder an enemy's attacks.

Prerequisite(s): Dex 15+, Dodge, base attack bonus +2 or Perform (dance) 2 ranks, elf.

Benefit(s): At the beginning of your turn, you can designate an opponent and receive a +2 dodge bonus to your Armor Class against attacks from that opponent, or you can designate two opponents and receive a +1 dodge bonus to your AC against each of them. You can change your designated opponent or opponents at every turn.

Using this feat relies on both movement and flowing garments, so you may not apply your dodge bonus from Battledancing when entangled, bound, grappling, or otherwise hampered, or if you are wearing armor that's not made mostly of cloth (e.g., padded armor or silken ceremonial armor).
feat-beast-speaker-mythic:
Even savage beasts willingly serve you if trained and well treated.

Prerequisite(s): Beast Speaker

Benefit(s): You are considered one level higher for all purposes related to the class feature that grants you a mount or companion. Your beast companion is considered a mythic creature and gains the hard to kill base mythic ability.

Whenever you expend a mythic surge your beast companion also gains a mythic surge that it can use at any time before the beginning of your next turn.

Special: You can select the mythic companion 1st-tier path ability, regardless of your path.
feat-beast-speaker-mastery-mythic:
You are able to drive your beast companion to perform amazing feats.

Prerequisite(s): Beast Speaker Mastery

Benefit(s): You are considered one level higher for all purposes related to the class feature that grants you a mount or companion; this stacks with the increase granted by Mythic Beast Speaker. Your beast companion also gains the recuperation base mythic ability. You may expend one use of your mythic power to allow your companion to use this ability to recover more quickly. You may expend one use of your mythic power as a full-round action to allow your beast companion to use the mythic version of any one feat it knows for 1 minute. If the mythic feat has effects that are not constant and require the use of mythic power, you must be adjacent to your beast companion (or riding it) and expend your mythic power to allow it to use these abilities. You can change the mythic feat your companion possesses by expending one use of mythic power; it may only gain one mythic bonus feat in this way.

Special: You can select any pact abilities that improve an animal companion, regardless of your path. You still must have a higher enough tier to select each path ability.
feat-bio-etheric-veils-akashic:
Prerequisites(s): Con 13, 3rd-level veilweaver.

Benefit(s): When you gain the dying condition, as a free action that can be taken on your turn even if you are unconscious, you can select one of your shaped veils. The selected veil is destroyed and you automatically stabilize.

You take essence burn equal to the amount of essence invested in the destroyed veil and gain 1 hit point for each point of essence burn taken in this way. Additionally, when a veil you have shaped would take enough damage to be sundered, you can use an immediate action to instead take some or all of the damage yourself to prevent this. Damage taken in this way is not reduced by damage reduction or energy resistance, immunity and cannot be prevented or redirected further in any way.

You gain 1 point of essence.
feat-biomech-construct-psionic:
Prerequisite(s): Ability to manifest astral construct.

Benefit(s): Whenever you manifest astral construct, you may apply the biomech template* to any constructs created by this power. In addition, whenever you select an astral construct menu option, you may instead select an enhancement menu option or abilities menu option of the corresponding level from the metamorphosis line of powers (for example, exchanging an option from Astral

Construct Menu A for an option from Abilities Menu A).
feat-biomech-pilot:
Prerequisite(s): Knowledge (nature) 1 rank, bonded mech* or ability to craft a mech.

Benefit(s): Your mech is at least partially biological, if not completely so, and as a result has access to many additional abilities. Such entities are known as "biomechs" and possess the biomech template*. The following Mech Enhancements can be selected by a mech pilot with this feat in addition to regular Mech Enhancements: Adrenaline Surge: The mech gains the ferocity universal monster ability.

• Accessible Physiology: For the purpose of spells and powers, the mech pilot may treat their mech as either construct or one of humanoid, aberration, or plant (chosen when this enhancement is selected), whichever is most beneficial.

• Feral Mech: The mech treats all integrated light melee weapons as natural attacks for the purpose of feats and other abilities.

• Gushing Fluid: When damaged, the mech violently pours forth vitriolic fluid that hoses its attacker. When the mech takes damage from a slashing or piercing weapon, all creatures adjacent to the mech must succeed at a Reflex save (DC is 10 + the mech's Hit Dice + the pilot's Strength modifier) or take acid damage as its caustic fluids spray forth. A mech deals an amount of acid damage in this way based on its size (1d4 points of acid damage for a Medium or smaller mech, 1d6 for a Large mech, 1d8 for a Huge mech, 2d6 for a Gargantuan mech, and 3d6 for a Colossal mech).

• Improved Feral Mech: The mech gains the pounce ability, but only with integrated weapons. The pilot must be at least 11th level and must have given the mech the feral Mech Enhancement to select this enhancement.

• Instinctive Action: If the mech's pilot becomes unconscious, stunned, or otherwise unable to pilot the mech, the mech continues to repeat the last action that it performed, attacking the nearest creature if it attacked or running if it ran. The mech is considered to have an intelligence score of – and a Wisdom score of 10 while acting in this way.

• Tissue Regeneration: The mech gains fast healing equal to 1/2 its HD, its biological components pulling themselves together under stress. The mech can heal up to 2 hit points per pilot level per day with this ability, after which it ceases to function.

Special: If you possess this feat as well as the ability to craft constructs, you may craft constructs with the biomech template and create mechs that use the Mech Enhancements listed above.
feat-bleeding-channel:
When you channel negative energy to harm a living creature, dozens of tiny gashes slice into the creature's skin, spilling its blood. These wounds are resistant to mundane healing.

Prerequisite(s): Channel negative energy 2d6 class feature, must have studied Memory Shards

Benefit(s): When you channel to harm living creatures, myriad cuts open on the victim's skin. If a creature fails its Will save, it takes an amount of bleed damage equal to 1/2 the number of dice of damage your channeled negative energy deals.
feat-blind-faith-monster:
Prerequisites(s): Iron Will, outsider type.

Benefit(s): You gain a +4 bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects. If you have at least 16 Hit Dice, you are immune to mind-affecting effects.
feat-blinded-awareness:
Without your sight, you grow more aware of the world around you.

Prerequisite(s): Elevated awareness racial trait, character level 9th.

Benefit: While your eyes are closed or you are otherwise blinded, the range of your blindsense increases to 30 feet and you gain blindsight 15 feet.
feat-bloodletter-combat:
Blood flows freely when you catch your enemies off guard.

Prerequisite(s): Bleeding attack rogue talent, sneak attack +3d6.

Benefit(s): Whenever you successfully sneak attack a target that is taking bleed damage, your sneak attack damage is increased by 1d6.
feat-bold-enforcer:
Your forceful will blends with your mental focus for enhanced effects.

Prerequisite(s): Will Enforcement spell-like ability, character level 9

Benefit(s): Whenever you use will enforcement, you may apply bold foci you know on the target as part of the enforcement effect. Numerical effects of bold foci applied in this way that normally equal the penalty of the hypnotic focus follow the rules of will enforcement instead. R number of bold foci may be active in this way at a time equal to your primary ability score bonus, distributed at will across the targets. If you run out of uses, you cannot benefit further from this feat until your will enforcement ends on at least one affected target.
feat-bonded-expert:
You are adept at using your bonded armor.

Prerequisite(s): Bonded armor class feature.

Benefit(s): You gain an additional use of your bonded armor's ability to summon itself, and your anima gains an additional use of teleport anima.
feat-bonded-holy-symbol:
Your holy symbol is imbued with special magics that bind your essence to it.

Prerequisite(s): Ability to cast divine spells

Benefit(s): You form a powerful bond with a holy symbol, which functions identically to a wizard's bonded object except it can be used to cast spells of your divine casting class (instead of wizard spells) and you can grant your bonded holy symbol only magic abilities appropriate for a holy symbol or a neck slot item. As with a wizard's bonded item, you can add additional magic abilities to your bonded holy symbol as if he had the required item creation feat (typically Craft Wondrous Item), provided you meet the feat's level prerequisites. The magic properties of a bonded holy symbol, including any magic abilities added to the object, function only for you. If a bonded holy symbol's owner dies or the item is replaced, the object loses all enhancements added using this ability.
feat-boon-mech:
Prerequisite(s): Bonded mech*, effective 3rd-level pilot for at least one mech.

Benefit(s): The abilities of your mech or companion vehicle are calculated as though your class were 4 levels higher, to a maximum effective pilot level equal to your character level. If you have more than one mech or companion vehicle, choose one to receive this benefit. If you lose or replace your mech or companion vehicle, you can apply this feat to the replacement.

Special: You can select this feat multiple times. The effects do not stack. Each time you take the feat, it applies to a different mech or companion vehicle.
feat-breaching-leap-mythic:
You can hurl your body out of the water up and over obstacles and creatures, and even crash down on those below.

Prerequisite(s): Str 13, swim speed.

Benefit(s): While swimming, you are always considered to have a running start when using Acrobatics to jump, and you gain a bonus on such checks equal to your mythic rank or tier. In addition, when making using the run or withdraw action or making a charge attack, you can expend one use of mythic power to include a single Acrobatics check made to jump, adding 10 feet per rank or tier to the height or distance you jump. You take no falling damage from the height gained as part of this leap. If you charge while using this feat and your attack hits, you may deal an amount of additional damage equal to the falling damage appropriate for the height you reached. Alternatively, you may replace your melee attack from this charge with a grapple check.

If you successfully grapple a creature, you bring it down to the water with you at the end of your jump, and it takes an appropriate amount of falling damage for the height it was at when you grappled it.
feat-breath-weapon-admixture-breath:
Breath Feats: A new category of feats, these feats serve to alter a wyrmtouched's breath weapon. Some of these feats reduce the damage die of your breath weapon while being used, indicated on the following table: This reduction applies to all damage dice the breath weapon deals (a 5th level wyrmtouched with 14 Constitution who applied the Breath Weapon Artisan feat to their breath weapon would deal 2d4+2 damage rather than 2d6+2). These feats can be combined, but the reduction to the breath weapon's damage die is cumulative and a breath feat cannot be applied if it would reduce the damage of a breath weapon below 1d1. Breath feats are marked with the [Breath] tag. Dragons are treated as though they had the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purpose of qualifying for breath feats and treat their hit dice as their character level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.

The elemental energy which brews in you is far more complex than most.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic breath weapon racial trait, character level 7th.

Benefit: Select an energy type (or physical damage types if you possess the Enigmatic Origins feat) which your breath weapon does not deal; you may now use that energy type with your breath weapon. In addition, you can mix any two damage types you may use with your breath weapon, causing your breath weapon to deal both types of damage; creatures take full damage from this breath weapon if they are not immune to or resist both damage types. Using this feat reduces the damage die of your breath weapon by 1 step (2 steps if one of the energy types is sonic).

Special: If you apply the Advanced Breath Weapon feat to your breath weapon in addition to this feat, any foe who fails their saving throw against your breath weapon suffers the effects of both conditions imposed by that feat.
feat-breath-weapon-artisan-breath:
Breath Feats: A new category of feats, these feats serve to alter a wyrmtouched's breath weapon. Some of these feats reduce the damage die of your breath weapon while being used, indicated on the following table: This reduction applies to all damage dice the breath weapon deals (a 5th level wyrmtouched with 14 Constitution who applied the Breath Weapon Artisan feat to their breath weapon would deal 2d4+2 damage rather than 2d6+2). These feats can be combined, but the reduction to the breath weapon's damage die is cumulative and a breath feat cannot be applied if it would reduce the damage of a breath weapon below 1d1. Breath feats are marked with the [Breath] tag. Dragons are treated as though they had the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purpose of qualifying for breath feats and treat their hit dice as their character level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.

Your talent at wielding your breath weapon is awe inspiring.

Prerequisite(s): Expanded Breath Weapon, character level 5th.

Benefit: You may modify your breath weapon by changing the area's shape to either a cylinder (10-foot radius, 30 feet high), a 40-foot cone, four 10-foot cubes, a ball (20-foot-radius spread), or a 120-foot line. Your breath weapon cannot travel more than 120 feet from your square. Using this feat reduces the damage die of your breath weapon by 1 step.

feat-browbeat-enforcement:
You break down mental defenses with your potent will.

Prerequisite(s): Will enforcement spell-like ability.

Benefit(s): You can use will enforcement without applying the will effect. The target may submit to the will effect to suppress the enforcement as normal. Using will enforcement in this way expends a daily use of the ability but does not expend a spell slot.
feat-brutal-follow-through-combat:
When you land a decisive blow, you know how to make it count.

Prerequisites: Power Attack, sneak attack +2d6.

Benefit(s): Whenever you score a critical hit with a weapon while using the Power Attack feat, you also deal additional damage as though your attack was a sneak attack. If the attack would qualify as a sneak attack, instead you add 2d6 to your sneak attack damage.
feat-careful-breath-weapon-breath:
Breath Feats: A new category of feats, these feats serve to alter a wyrmtouched's breath weapon. Some of these feats reduce the damage die of your breath weapon while being used, indicated on the following table: This reduction applies to all damage dice the breath weapon deals (a 5th level wyrmtouched with 14 Constitution who applied the Breath Weapon Artisan feat to their breath weapon would deal 2d4+2 damage rather than 2d6+2). These feats can be combined, but the reduction to the breath weapon's damage die is cumulative and a breath feat cannot be applied if it would reduce the damage of a breath weapon below 1d1. Breath feats are marked with the [Breath] tag. Dragons are treated as though they had the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purpose of qualifying for breath feats and treat their hit dice as their character level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.

Through technique and training, you have made your breath weapon less dangerous to those around you.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic breath weapon racial trait.

Benefit: When you use your breath weapon, you may choose a number of spaces equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1); these spaces are unaffected by your breath weapon.
feat-careful-reader-mythic:
The written word cannot hurt someone of your mythic stature.

Prerequisite: Careful Reader.

Benefit: Your bonus on saving throws against written magical effects from Careful Reader doubles. By expending one use of mythic power, you can roll such a saving throw again and choose the best result.
feat-cast-rune:
Even if you are not a practitioner of rune magic, you are protected by a specific rune present in your name or influencing your day of birth.

Benefit: Select one rune as per the Patron Rune trait. You may invoke your patron rune once per day to gain its benefits, as listed under "Runic Divination". The rune's effects last for 1 hour, or until you use its granted power once (whatever happens first).

Special: You can gain this feat multiple times. Its effects do not stack. Each time you take the feat, it grants a new rune you can invoke.
feat-celestial-familiar:
You open a conduit to the upper planes to invest your familiar with its essence.

Prerequisite(s): Familiar, 5th level, non-evil alignment

Benefit(s): Your familiar gains the celestial simple template, though its type remains unchanged. If you gain an improved familiar, that familiar also gains this template unless it possesses the evil subtype.

Special: A familiar cannot gain both the celestial and fiendish simple templates.
feat-cetacean-smash-mythic:
You can hurl your body with devastating force, leaping out of the water and crashing down on your enemies.

Prerequisite(s): Large or larger size, swim speed.

Benefit(s): While swimming, you are always considered to have a running start when using Acrobatics to jump, and you can use your Strength modifier in place of your Dexterity modifier on such checks. In addition, you can use this feat to hurl your body out of the water to land on foes three or more sizes smaller as a standard action, using your whole body to crush them. This attack affects as many creatures as fit within your space, dealing damage based on your size plus 1-1/2 times your Strength modifier. When attacking objects or structures, you ignore an amount of their hardness equal to your mythic rank or tier.

Size Damage

Large 2d6

Huge 2d8

Gargantuan 4d6

Colossal 4d8

If at least half your body lands out of the water when making a cetacean smash, you fall prone. However, creatures damaged by your leap are pinned under you unless they succeed on a Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 your Hit Dice + your Strength modifier). Pinned creatures take bludgeoning damage each round they end their turn still pinned. You must make a combat maneuver check on your turn to maintain the pin, though you do not take a penalty on this check for being prone.

If you land on creatures in the water, they are not pinned but instead are staggered for 1 round and pushed 1d6 x 5 feet below the water's surface. If they strike a solid obstruction while being pushed in this way, they take 1d6 points of damage per 10 feet they were pushed.

If you expend one use of your mythic power, you can affect creatures two sizes smaller with your cetacean smash. If you expend two uses, you can affect creatures one size smaller.
feat-chain-collectives-psionic-teamwork:
Prerequisite(s): Collective class feature.

Benefit(s): Whenever you and an ally both possess this feat and the collective class feature and both belong to each other's collectives, you may treat any creatures in your ally's collective as being in your own collective, even if this would cause the normal limit on members and range to be exceeded.
feat-challenge-study:
Your challenge is far more nuanced than others.

Prerequisite(s): Legendary Cavalier 1st, challenge aspect.

Benefit(s): Select 1 order from the cavalier base class (rather than those available to the legendary cavalier); you gain the challenge ability listed in that order's description.
feat-channel-radiance-mythic:
The divine radiance of your channeled energy is blinding and a bane for darkness and evil.

Prerequisite(s): Channel Radiance.

Benefit(s): The radiance summoned when you channel positive energy functions now as mythic brightest light.
feat-channeled-breath-weapon-breath:
Breath Feats: A new category of feats, these feats serve to alter a wyrmtouched's breath weapon. Some of these feats reduce the damage die of your breath weapon while being used, indicated on the following table: This reduction applies to all damage dice the breath weapon deals (a 5th level wyrmtouched with 14 Constitution who applied the Breath Weapon Artisan feat to their breath weapon would deal 2d4+2 damage rather than 2d6+2). These feats can be combined, but the reduction to the breath weapon's damage die is cumulative and a breath feat cannot be applied if it would reduce the damage of a breath weapon below 1d1. Breath feats are marked with the [Breath] tag. Dragons are treated as though they had the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purpose of qualifying for breath feats and treat their hit dice as their character level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.

Rather than using your elemental might as a weapon, you instead suffuse it into your weapon.`

Prerequisite(s): Draconic breath weapon racial trait.

Benefit: As a swift action, you may expend a use of your breath weapon to instead channel its power into one weapon you are currently wielding, causing it to deal an additional +1d6 damage of that element for a number of rounds equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). At 8th level and again at 16th, this additional damage increases by +1d6.

Special: Using this feat is treated as using your breath weapon, requiring you to wait 1 round before you can use it again.
feat-channeling-blast-mythic:
Your deity exerts its will through your destructive energy.

Prerequisite(s): Channeling Blast.

Benefit(s): You gain the mythic version of the channeling feat you selected for the non-mythic Channeling Blast, or you can choose another non-mythic channeling feat.
feat-channeling-kinesis-mythic:
You are a vehicle for divine energy in the natural world.

Prerequisite(s): Channeling Kinesis.

Benefit(s): Your negative or positive blast counts as the channel energy ability for all prerequisites.
feat-charismatic-caster:
In your secret identity, you dabble in magical music and bardic spells.

Prerequisite: Cabalist, warlock, or zealot 1st.

Benefit(s): You now cast as a spontaneous caster (if you didn't already), using the bard's spells known to determine how many spells you know, as well as no longer needing a spellbook to prepare your spells. You also use your Charisma modifier instead of your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier to determine your ability to cast spells, bonus spells, spell DCS, and other related spell effects.

Special: This feat must be selected at 1st level, or before your first level of cabalist, warlock, or zealot. A cabalist, warlock, or zealot can choose to gain this feat in place of their 1st level social talent. A zealot who takes this feat also uses their Charisma in place of their Wisdom for all abilities related to their inquisition.

Special: You cannot select this feat if you possess the Genius Vigilante feat.
feat-clever-ropework:
With a length of rope, chain, or a whip, you can restrict your foe's movement.

Benefit(s): As a standard action you may make a melee touch attack against a target within 15 feet as long as you are holding a similar length of rope, chain, or a whip. If this touch attack succeeds you move adjacent to your target and wrap your rope around their legs, rendering the target entangled. The target can still move and may free themselves as normal using Escape Artist or making a Strength check to burst their bonds as normal for whatever material is binding them such as when they have been ensnared in a net.
feat-collective-dominion-proxy-psionic:
Prerequisites(s): Enhancement sphere, Circle Casting, Spell Proxy, casting class feature, collective class feature, magic skill bonus +10.

Benefit(s): The benefits of your Proxy feats apply to creatures within your collective regardless of range. This does not allow them to use the Circle Casting feat from beyond the normal range.
feat-collective-manabond-psionic:
Prerequisites(s): Mana sphere, collective class feature.

Benefit(s): Whenever you add a creature to your collective, you may create a manabond with them as if you had cast a Mana sphere ability. When you concentrate on a single manabond created in this way, you are treated as concentrating on all manabonds created through this feat.

A manabond created through this feat ends immediately if the creature leaves your collective.
feat-combat-breath-weapon-breath:
Breath Feats: A new category of feats, these feats serve to alter a wyrmtouched's breath weapon. Some of these feats reduce the damage die of your breath weapon while being used, indicated on the following table: This reduction applies to all damage dice the breath weapon deals (a 5th level wyrmtouched with 14 Constitution who applied the Breath Weapon Artisan feat to their breath weapon would deal 2d4+2 damage rather than 2d6+2). These feats can be combined, but the reduction to the breath weapon's damage die is cumulative and a breath feat cannot be applied if it would reduce the damage of a breath weapon below 1d1. Breath feats are marked with the [Breath] tag. Dragons are treated as though they had the draconic breath weapon racial trait for the purpose of qualifying for breath feats and treat their hit dice as their character level for the purpose of meeting prerequisites.

Even in the thick of battle, you can wield your breath weapon without missing a step.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic breath weapon racial trait, character level 5th.

Benefit: You gain the ability to use your breath weapon in different circumstances:

• Whenever you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 standard action, you may use your breath weapon as a swift action. Using this feat in this way reduces the damage die of your breath weapon by 3 steps.

• Whenever you make an attack action, you may use your breath weapon as a swift action. Using this feat in this way reduces the damage die of your breath weapon by 2 steps.

Normal: You can use your breath weapon as a standard action.
feat-combatants-alignment-combat:
Prerequisites(s): Essence sphere (Parallel Alignment (potent)), ability to gain martial focus.

Benefit(s): Select a second parallel alignment which replaces either your normal alignment or your parallel alignment as long as you have martial focus.
feat-command-alignment-mythic:
You can command creatures of your same alignment.

Prerequisites(s): Command Alignment.

Benefit(s): Your command alignment ability affects any creatures with the same alignment as those affected by non-mythic Command Alignment (not just outsiders, neither just those with that alignment subtype), but these targets gain a +4 bonus on their Will save unless they have an aura of that alignment (like clerics, paladins and warpriests). Alternatively, you can expend two uses of mythic power when using Command Alignment to affect all targets of the chosen alignment as if they had that alignment subtype.
feat-confusing-critical-combat-critical-:
You can make your foes confused with a weapon blow at will.

Prerequisite(s): Confusing Critical, 3rd mythic tier.

Benefit(s): Once per round when you hit a foe with an attack, but the attack is not a critical, you may expend two uses of mythic power to inflict the effect of the Confusing Critical feat rather than your attack's normal damage.

You may not add the effects of more than one mythic critical feat to a single attack.
feat-confusing-critical-combat-critical:
Your critical hits cause confusion in your opponents.

Prerequisite(s): Staggering Critical, base attack bonus +17.

Benefit(s): Whenever you score a critical hit, your opponent becomes confused for 1d4 rounds. A successful Fortitude save reduces the duration to 1 round. The DC of this Fortitude save is equal to 10 + your base attack bonus. The effects of this feat do not stack. Additional hits instead add to the duration.

Special: You can only apply the effects of one critical feat to a given critical hit unless you possess Critical Mastery.
feat-consecrate-spell-like-ability-monst:
Your spell-like ability is most efficacious on evil creatures.

Prerequisites: Good subtype, spell-like ability at caster level 5th or higher.

Benefit: Choose one of your spell-like abilities, subject to the restrictions described in this feat. You can use the chosen spell-like ability as a consecrate spell-like ability up to three times per day (or less, if the ability is normally usable only once or twice per day).

A consecrated spell-like ability is treated as a maximized spell-like ability against evil creatures and creatures with the evil subtype. Against all other creatures, this feat does not modify the spell in any way (for example, a consecrated fireball acts as a normal fireball against neutral or good creatures). This feat does not stack with Maximize Spell-Like Ability.

You can only select a spell-like ability duplicating a spell with a level less than or equal to ½ your caster level –2.

Special: This feat can be taken multiple times. Each time it is taken, you can apply it to a different spell-like ability.
feat-contagious-power-metapsionic:
Benefit(s): To use this feat, you must expend your psionic focus. This feat can be applied only to powers that are harmful to their target and do not have a range of personal; a contagious power never spreads to someone who would benefit from being the target of the power.

A manifester level check to dispel or remove a contagious power that fails by 5 or more causes it to spread from the original target to the creature that attempted to remove it.

The power spreads to the new target regardless of its normal range or any special targeting requirement like a melee or ranged touch attack. The power is treated as if you had just manifested it on the new target.

The new target receives a saving throw as well as the benefit of power resistance (if applicable) if the power normally allows it. A contagious power can be identified normally as it is being cast with a successful Spellcraft check. Identifying whether a power is contagious by its effect, however, requires the use of the aura sight power, analyze dweomer spell, or a similar effect. Using this feat increases the power point cost of the power by 2. The power's total cost cannot exceed your manifester level.
feat-contingent-injection:
Prerequisite: Heal 11 ranks.

Benefit(s): When you inject a creature with a pharmaceutical, poison, stimulant*, or other injection, you can delay the effect of the injection by up to 1 day. You may set some condition which causes the injection to activate on command. A creature can only have one contingent injection at any given time.
feat-covert-disassembly:
Prerequisite: Any item creation feat.

Benefit(s): You can break any non-cursed magic or technological item down into component pieces. These pieces are non-magical and nontechnological and may have little resemblance to the original item other than being of the same material (a magical sword may be three recognizable metal pieces or simply a collection of metal scraps). Disassembling an item takes 1 hour per 1,000 gp of the item's price and requires you to concentrate as if crafting an item. You can only use this feat on items your item creation feat would let you craft (for example, if you have Craft Wondrous Item, you can disassemble wondrous items but not magic weapons or armor).

You may reassemble a dismantled item as long as all the pieces are present; this takes the same amount of time as taking it apart did.
feat-craft-cursed-item:
You may intentionally craft a cursed item as if you were crafting a regular magic item.

Prerequisite(s): Caster level 3rd.

Benefit: You can create a wide variety of cursed items.

Crafting a cursed item takes 1 day for each 1,000 gp in the normal item's price. To create a cursed item, you must use up raw materials costing half of its base price. You may create cursed armor, weapons, and wondrous items with this feat.

You can also place a curse upon an existing magic item if it is one that you could make. Doing so costs half the raw materials and half the time it would take to craft that item.
feat-craft-mech-item-creation:
Prerequisites(s): Craft (mechanical) 11 ranks, Knowledge (engineering) 11 ranks, Technologist*.

Benefit(s): You can create mechs. Any character with access to the vehicle's key or other control mechanism may drive and use this vehicle. Creating a mech takes 1 week for every 1,000 gp in the item's price. To create the object, you must use up raw materials costing half of this total price. See Non-Companion Mechs for more information. You can repair a broken mech if it is one that you could make. Doing so costs half the raw materials and half the time it would take to craft the mech from scratch.

Special: A military lab is required to craft mechs and uses 100 charges each day it is in operation.
feat-craft-stimulant-item-creation:
Prerequisite(s): Caster or manifester level 5th.

Benefit(s): You can create stimulants*. Crafting a stimulant takes 1 day for each 1,000 gp in its base price. To craft a stimulant, you must use up raw materials costing half of its base price.
feat-cross-specialization-combat:
You are versatile in your abilities.

Prerequisite(s): 11th level vigilante.

Benefit(s): You are treated as though you possessed either the avenger or stalker specialization for the purposes of which vigilante talents you can select, treating your character level as your vigilante level -4 when selecting vigilante talents with this feat, but for the purpose of the vigilante talents effect, your effective vigilante level is equal to your full character level.

Normal: You must select the avenger or stalker vigilante specialization to select talent which require the stated specialization.
feat-crossblooded-disciple:
Your heritages develop almost at the same pace.

Prerequisite(s): Crossblooded sorcerer or crossblooded rager archetype, bloodline disciple level 1.

Benefit(s): Choose one bloodline you possess that doesn't advance its powers with your bloodline disciple levels (it can't be one you gained through Eldritch Heritage). Your bloodline disciple levels stack with your sorcerer or bloodrager levels when determining the powers gained from this bloodline. You still can't gain new powers through level increase from a bloodline you didn't select for your bloodline disciple subclass.
feat-crystal-psiborg-psionic:
Prerequisite(s): Psicrystal Affinity*, manifester level 1st.

Benefit(s): Your psicrystal transforms into a single piece of psibertech*, granting you the base augmentation of that psibertech component. The psicrystal is now attached to your body and can no longer move or leave your body (assuming it ever could), but gains hardness equal to 5 + 1/2 your manifester level. A psibertech psicrystal still grants all the normal benefits for being within 5 feet of you (such as the Alertness feat) and continues to function if the psicrystal is consumed or integrated as a result of another feat or class feature (such as the crystal warrior's form astral suit class feature or the Mech Piloting* feat).
feat-cultic-opiate:
Your cultic tradition achieves deeper communion with its patrons through the use of mind-altering substances.

Prerequisite(s): Craft (alchemy) 1 rank

Benefit(s): Choose one druggmg.

When you use this substance, you attain an almost supernatural openness to your patron.

As long as the drug is providing a beneficial effect, you gain a +1 bonus to one of the following categories: attack rolls; caster level checks and concentration checks; saving throws; or skill checks. If you are good-aligned, this is a sacred bonus; if you are evil, it is a profane bonus. If you are neutral, you must choose which type of bonus to receive; once chosen, it cannot be altered. You take a -2 penalty to saving throws related to addiction against your chosen drug.
feat-deadly-disappearance-combat:
Your opponents lose track of you in the carnage of battle when you land a telling blow.

Prerequisite(s): Sneak attack +5d6, Stealth 10 ranks

Benefit(s): When attacking a creature you flank or that is denied its Dexterity bonus, if you confirm a critical hit against that opponent or reduce that creature to 0 hit points or fewer, you can make a Stealth even while being directly observed and without cover or concealment. If your Stealth check succeeds, you gain total concealment until the end of your next turn or until you attack.
feat-deadly-opportunist-combat:
Your opportunity attacks are deadly accurate.

Prerequisite(s): Combat Reflexes, opportunist rogue talent.

Benefit(s): You increase the critical threat range of any light weapon you wield by 1 when you are making attacks of opportunity. In addition, when you confirm a critical hit with a slight weapon when making an attack of opportunity, you can make an additional attack with the same weapon against the same target as an immediate action.
feat-dedicate-of-ascension:
Prerequisite: Knowledge (history) 3 ranks.

Benefit(s): Choose a path of ascension*. Each path of ascension requires a different initial meditation which takes 8 hours. Once you have performed the meditation, you gain the benefit of a special ability or resistance as indicated in the meditation entry for the path of ascension for which you have performed the meditation. If you have at least 12 Hit Dice, you also gain the first boon granted by your path of ascension. If you have at least 16 Hit Dice, you also gain the second boon. If you have 20 Hit Dice or more, you also gain the third boon.

Unless a specific duration or number of uses per day is listed, a boon's effects are constant. If you have levels in the ascendant vanguard prestige class, you gain access to these boons at lower levels as a benefit of your prestige class.
feat-defensive-archery:
You are adept at making shots while dodging attackers trying to stop you.

Prerequisite(s): Point-Blank Shot

Benefit(s): You gain a +4 dodge bonus to AC against attacks of opportunity triggered by your ranged attack.

Special: A fighter may select this feat as a fighter bonus combat feat.
feat-defensive-scales:
Your scales provide you a measure of protection against all blows.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic scales or adamantine scales racial trait, character level 3rd.

Benefit: You gain DR 3/magic.

Special: If you possess the adamantine scales racial trait, this DR is increased by 2.
feat-defile-spell-metamagic:
You infuse spells with corrupt fiendish power, drastically increasing their effectiveness against good creatures.

Prerequisites: Evil alignment, able to prepare or cast desecrate.

Benefit: A defiled spell is treated as a maximized spell against good creatures and creatures with the good subtype.

Against all other creatures, this feat does not modify the spell in any way (for example, a defiled lightning bolt acts as a normal lightning bolt against neutral or evil creatures).

This feat does not stack with Maximize Spell.

Level Increase: +2 (a defiled spell uses up a spell slot two levels higher than the spell's actual level.)
feat-destructive-study:
Your counsel can help destroy your foes.

Prerequisite(s): Reduced commander's aura class feature, Aura Study or Order Study.

Benefit(s): You gain access to the destructive counsel aura.
feat-devastating-breath-mythic:
Your breath unleashes an irresistible holocaust of destruction.

Prerequisite(s): Con 19, breath weapon special attack.

Benefit(s): Your breath weapon ignores the energy resistance of non-mythic creatures and the hardness of non-mythic objects. Non-mythic creatures with immunity to the energy type of your breath weapon take half damage, save that creatures with the cold subtype or fire subtype take no damage from breath weapons of that energy type. You are always immune to your own breath weapon. A creature that has vulnerability against the energy type of your breath weapon takes double damage instead of 150% normal damage.

If you expend one use of your mythic power as a free action when using your breath weapon, you also affect mythic creatures as described above, and your breath weapon bypasses the energy immunity of non-mythic creatures (except creatures with the cold and fire subtypes against cold or fire damage, respectively).
feat-devil-mantis-form:
You can take the form of a fiendish mantis.

Prerequisites: Crimson assassin 8th.

Benefit(s): You can temporarily increase the power of your mantis form. When in blood mantis form, you can spend a swift action to gain bonuses as if you had the fiendish template. In addition to the energy resistances, your damage reduction increases to DR 10/good, and you gain SR equal to your character level + 4, as well as the smite good ability. You can maintain devil mantis form for a number of rounds equal to your crimson assassin level. These rounds do not need to be used consecutively and can be used in 1 round increments. Devil mantis form can be dismissed as a free action, returning you to blood mantis form.
feat-disfiguring-transformation: Benefit(s): Whenever you apply a graft, piece of cybertech, or polymorph effect to a creature, you may warp their appearance in some manner that makes them unpleasant to gaze on. For as long as they are affected, the target creature takes a -4 penalty to all Charisma checks and Charisma-based skill checks.
feat-dislocate-mythic:
You don't fear pain if this can help setting you free.

Prerequisite(s): Dislocate.

Benefit(s): You can apply the benefits of Dislocate both to Escape Artist checks or combat maneuver checks to escape a grapple.

You add your mythic tier as a bonus on all these checks. Lastly, when you would suffer nonlethal damage by using Dislocate, you can delay this damage by a number of rounds equal to your mythic tier.
feat-dislocated-form-psionic: Benefit(s): While maintaining psionic focus, you gain the compression universal monster ability, and take only half damage from being crushed. You may expend psionic focus to gain DR/- equal to your level against nonlethal damage until the start of your next turn.
feat-divergent-visionary-mythic:
Prerequisite(s): Divination sphere, caster level 9th; or ability to cast one divination spell of 5th level or higher or manifest one clairsentience power of 5th level or higher.

Benefit(s): Any of your clairsentience powers or divination spells or Divination talents which function across planes now also function across alternate timelines and separations in time. For example, a character with the telepathic bond spell active can send messages to an ally they are aware of who is currently in an alternate timeline or even in an alternate time period in that timeline (such as 100 years in the past). Likewise, a character could use scrying to look at a location at a different point in time in another timeline they are aware of.

You must be aware of a specific alternate timeline's existence (such as having traveled from it, knowing that somebody else has traveled to it, or knowing that a portal exists to it) in order to target that timeline or anything in it. An alternate "stripe" of time resulting from an inconsequential form of time travel (such as using a Shadowbore or teleportation effect for superluminal travel) does not qualify as an alternate timeline.

Note: Even in a game which involves players crossing multiple alternate universes, GMs may wish to restrict the ability of players to cross between timelines they know of. As a result, players wishing to take this feat should gain approval from their GM beforehand.
feat-divine-communion-mythic:
Your will is one with the will of your deity.

Prerequisite(s): Divine Communion

Benefit(s): You add 1/2 your mythic tier to the number of times per day you can use Divine Communion. If you expend one use of mythic power, you double the insight bonus you gain on Wisdom.
feat-divine-expression-mythic:
Divine power and artistic expression complement each other.

Prerequisite(s): Divine Expression, 3rd mythic tier.

Benefits: Your bard level stacks with your cleric or oracle level for the purpose of gaining new types of bardic performance.
feat-draconic-heritage-mythic:
Your draconic characteristics become stronger and mythic.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic Heritage.

Benefit(s): You add 1/2 your mythic tier to the number of times per day you can use the ability granted by your draconic heritage. In addition, if you are 3th tier or more, you gain an additional ability depending on your dragon type.

• Chromatic: Your unarmed attacks' damage is calculated in d8 rather than d6.

• Esoteric: Your psychic barrage dazes an opponent for 1 round per 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Imperial: The radius of your aura of command increases by 5 ft. for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Land: The radius of your aura of calm increases by 5 ft. for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Metallic: Your resistance to your chosen element increases by 5 for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Outer: The radius of your alien aura increases by 5 ft. for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Planar: The radius of your planar aura increases by 5 ft. for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Primal: The radius of your elemental aura increases by 5 ft. for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Drake: Your bonus speed increases by 5 ft. for every 2 mythic tiers you possess.

• Linnorm: The effects of your curse last for 1 round per 2 mythic tiers you possess.
feat-draconic-manifestation-mythic:
When manifesting your draconic claws, you unlock tremendous power.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic Manifestation.

Benefit(s): You add your mythic tier to your level for the purpose of determining the effects (but not the duration) of your draconic manifestation. You also add ½ your mythic tier (minimum 1) to the number of rounds per day you can use your draconic manifestation.
feat-draconic-tail-combat-mythic:
Your tail becomes a deadly energy weapon.

Prerequisite(s): Draconic Tail.

Benefit(s): Your tail attack deals damage as if you were one size larger. If your claw attacks deal energy damage, your tail deals 1d6 additional points of energy damage too.
feat-draconic-tail-combat:
You grow a dragon's tail while fighting.

Prerequisite(s): Access to natural claw attacks, bloodrager or sorcerer with the draconic bloodline, base attack bonus +5, Draconic Manifestation.

Benefit(s): Whenever you manifest your claws, you also gain a tail slap attack. This is a secondary attack dealing 1d6 points of damage (1d4 if you are Small), plus 1—½ times your Strength modifier.
feat-draconic-wild-shape:
You can change into a draconic animal.

Prerequisite(s): Wild shape class feature, Knowledge (arcana) 5 ranks.
